reader_summary.headline: Business Breakdowns is a series of conversations with investors and operators diving deep into a single business.
reader_summary.overview: Business Breakdowns is a series of conversations with investors and operators diving deep into a single business. For each business, we explore its history, its business model, its competitive advantages, and what makes it tick? We believe every business has lessons and secrets that investors and operators can learn from, and we are here to bring them to you.

thesis: This episode argues that Sherwin-Williams is a superior, vertically integrated business with a unique distribution model that creates intense loyalty among professional painters and exclusive access to major builders. The speaker highlights the company's low capital intensity, consistent free cash flow generation, and strategic growth runway as key drivers of value, noting that while the stock may trade at a higher starting valuation, its structural advantages and management's long-term focus make it an attractive investment.

claims.claim: Sherwin-Williams dominates the professional paint market and controls a significant majority of it.
claims.quote: Overall, I estimate that Sherwin might control about 75% of the professional paint market. Good market to have that control over.

claims.claim: Sherwin-Williams has a unique controlled distribution model that makes it the only significant player with a vertically integrated business.
claims.quote: As I mentioned earlier, Sherwin's unique in the paint business, as it's truly the only player of significance that operates a controlled distribution or near vertically integrated business model.

claims.claim: Professional painters are extremely loyal to Sherwin-Williams, preferring it over the second largest brand by a large margin.
claims.quote: As a result, professional painter's are extremely loyal to Sherwin, prefering it over the number two brand Benjamin Moore by a margin of five to one.

claims.claim: Sherwin-Williams has exclusive agreements with the vast majority of top national home builders and property management companies.
claims.quote: It has exclusive agreements with 23 of the top 25 national home builders and 17 of the top 20 property management companies.

claims.claim: Sherwin-Williams has a remarkably low employee turnover rate at its stores compared to other retailers.
claims.quote: Annual employee turnover at stores is less than 10%, which is remarkably low for a retailer and highlights the quality of the service a painter can receive at Sherwin paint stores.

claims.claim: Sherwin-Williams maintains a controlled distribution model that generates intense loyalty from professional painters and allows for better pricing control.
claims.quote: Well, SGNA as a personal sales is around 30%, which is high relative to many peers, and that's because of Sherwin's controlled distribution model, and its willingness to invest heavily heavily in service for his professional painters.

claims.claim: Sherwin-Williams has low capital intensity with CapEx under 2% of sales and generates attractive tangible returns on invested capital.
claims.quote: The capital intensity of business is rather low with CAPX under 2% of sales. CapExx is primarily for new store openings, which are about 80, $80,200 per year, year, and also periodic expansion of manufacturing capacity.

claims.claim: Sherwin-Williams has a consistent policy of returning free cash flow to shareholders via dividends and buybacks without holding excess cash.
claims.quote: After M&A, Sherwin's always had a consistent policy that it will not hold excess cash, choosing to return to shareholders in the formable dividends and buybacks.

claims.claim: Management is long-term focused and willing to take on leverage to acquire businesses like Valspar to create substantial long-term value.
claims.quote: So this was a clear sign that management is long-term focused, willing to be patient and ignore the market short-term demands in order to create substantial long-term value for shareholders.

claims.claim: Masco's decorative architectural group has high teens operating margins and low cap-ex, but lower gross margins than Sherwin-Williams because it sells paint through other stores.
claims.quote: Masco has high teens operating margins, which compares to Sherwin's paint stores group in the low 20s. And Masco has equally low cap-ex, of course, without even the need to open stores.

claims.claim: Benjamin Moore had high teens operating margins prior to being acquired by Berkshire Hathaway, but its growth rates have been much lower than Sherwin-Williams.
claims.quote: And actually, the last time we got to look at Ben Morris financials financials, prior to Berkshire acquiring them, they also had high teens' operating margins by selling paint through other stores.

claims.claim: The speaker views Sherwin-Williams as a superior business that has historically been undervalued relative to peers, noting its resilience during housing downturns and its unique vertical integration model.
claims.quote: Therefore, paying a modest premium to the market or peers for far superior growth in returns with less risk, it seemed like a bargain. And as such, Sherwin's stock has compounded well in excess of the market and those peers over time, suggesting that its, quote, unquote, premium valuation was actually a discount.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that while the market now appreciates Sherwin more, future stock returns may be more modest given the higher starting valuation.
claims.quote: Today, I do think the market has developed a greater appreciation for some truly superior businesses such as Sherwin, and as such, perhaps future stock returns may be more modest, given a higher starting point with regards to to valuation, which is now close to the 30 times earnings.
